question_text: Find the mean deviation about the median for the following data: xᵢ = 6, 9, 3, 12, 15, 13, 21, 22; fᵢ = 4, 5, 3, 2, 5, 4, 4, 3.

mark_split.label: Find |xᵢ − M| and fᵢ|xᵢ − M| and their sum

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the mean deviation about the median for a discrete frequency table — what you do to the data first, how you locate the median, and what you divide at the end.
insider_note: Sort the data first and keep each frequency with its value; the median is read from the cumulative frequency column — the first c.f. at or above N/2 = 15 gives M = 13 — and the grouped-data formula with l and C is not used on discrete data.

steps.label: Ascending order and c.f.
steps.margin_note: First two marks. The data is NOT in order (6, 9, 3, 12, …), so the first move is to sort the xᵢ and carry each frequency with its value. Columns: xᵢ, fᵢ, cumulative frequency c.f.
lines: Ascending order of xᵢ, with the c.f.:

recall.must_convey: That the values are first sorted in ascending order with their frequencies, and a cumulative frequency column 3, 7, 12, 14, 18, 23, 27, 30 is written, N = 30.
accept: sort the x i in ascending order with their frequencies and write the cumulative frequency, three seven twelve fourteen eighteen twenty three twenty seven thirty
arrange the data in increasing order, keep each frequency with its value, add the frequencies to get c f, N thirty
first put the values in order then make the running total column ending at thirty
x i ni ascending order lo pettali, f i tho paatu, cumulative frequency rayali, N thirty
ascending order table with c f column, total thirty

steps.why: A median is the middle of the ORDERED data. Sorting first, and moving each frequency with its value, is the step that makes the cumulative frequency mean anything.
common_mistakes: Writing the c.f. for the data in the given (unsorted) order.
Sorting the xᵢ but leaving the fᵢ in their original order.

steps.label: Median
steps.margin_note: Next two marks. N/2 = 15. Reading down the c.f. column, 14 is below 15 and 18 is the first at or above it, so the 15th item is a 13. No interpolation for discrete data: the median IS that value.
lines: The first c.f. ≥ 15 is 18, at xᵢ = 13.

recall.must_convey: That N/2 = 15, the first cumulative frequency at or above 15 is 18, and so the median is the value there, M = 13.
accept: N by two is fifteen, the first c f at or above fifteen is eighteen, so the median is thirteen
the fifteenth item falls in the c f eighteen row which is x i equals thirteen
look for where the cumulative frequency first reaches fifteen, that value thirteen is the median
N by two fifteen, c f lo eighteen daggara vasthundi, median thirteen
median is thirteen

steps.why: For a discrete table each value occupies a block of positions; the c.f. column is the end of each block. N = 30 is even, so the median is the average of the 15th and 16th items — here both fall in the block of 13, so the median is 13. Read both positions: when a cumulative frequency lands exactly on N/2 the two middle items are different values and the median is their average.
common_mistakes: Using the grouped-data formula l + (C/f)(N/2 − m) on discrete data.
Taking the median as the middle of the xᵢ list (12 or 13 by position) and ignoring the frequencies.

steps.label: Deviations from the median
steps.margin_note: Next two marks. Columns: xᵢ, fᵢ, |xᵢ − 13|, and the product with fᵢ. The row xᵢ = 13 contributes 0. The sum is 149.

recall.must_convey: That each value's absolute deviation from 13 is found, multiplied by its frequency, and the products add to 149.
accept: subtract thirteen from each x i, take the absolute value, multiply by f i and add to get one forty nine
the deviations are ten seven four one zero two eight nine and the weighted sum is one hundred forty nine
find the absolute deviations from the median, weight them by frequency, total one forty nine
prathi x i nunchi thirteen teesi mod teesukoni f i tho multiply cheste sum one forty nine
sigma f i mod x i minus M is one hundred and forty nine

steps.why: Mean deviation averages DISTANCES from the median, so the sign of each deviation is dropped and the median's own row contributes nothing.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by the c.f. instead of by fᵢ.

steps.label: Mean deviation
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 149/30 = 4.9666…, written 4.97. Divide by N = 30, not by the 8 rows.
lines: M.D. about the median = Σfᵢ|xᵢ − M|/N

recall.must_convey: That the mean deviation about the median is Σfᵢ|xᵢ − M| divided by N: 149/30 = 4.97.
accept: mean deviation is one forty nine by thirty which is four point nine seven
divide the weighted sum by N thirty to get four point nine seven
M D about the median equals sigma f i mod x i minus M by N equals four point nine seven
one forty nine ni thirty tho divide cheste four point nine seven
the answer is four point nine seven

steps.why: The mean deviation is the average distance of an observation from the median. Dividing by N = 30 (all the observations, counted with frequency) is what makes it an average.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 8 (the number of rows) instead of 30.
Copying the book's slip 'median deviation' — the name is mean deviation about the median.
